selectedPapers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
selectedPapers.abstract:
While large language models (LLMs) have shown impressive performance across reasoning and decision making tasks, their ability to synergize reasoning and acting remains underexplored. We propose ReAct, a general framework to combine reasoning traces and task-specific actions.

This landmark research by Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao sets an empirical benchmark in Autonomous AI Agents. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

selectedPapers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
selectedPapers.abstract:
We introduce Tree of Thoughts (ToT), which generalizes over popular chain-of-thought prompting for language models. ToT enables deliberate problem solving by exploring multiple reasoning paths and self-evaluating choices.

This landmark research by Shunyu Yao, Dian Yu, Jeffrey Zhao, Izhak Shafran, Thomas L. Griffiths, Yuan Cao, Karthik Narasimhan sets an empirical benchmark in Factuality & Citation Grounding. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

selectedPapers.title: Nougat: Neural Optical Understanding for Academic PDF Parsing
selectedPapers.abstract:

This landmark research by Lukas Blecher, Guillaume Mialon, Thomas Scialom, Gaetan Loridant, Raphaël Thomas, Roman Pascal sets an empirical benchmark in Multimodal Vision & Document OCR. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

As human knowledge is predominantly stored in books and scientific articles, PDF visual extraction is critical. We present Nougat (Neural Optical Understanding for Academic Documents), a Visual Transformer model that converts scientific PDFs to lightweight markup.

This landmark research by Lukas Blecher, Guillaume Mialon, Thomas Scialom, Gaetan Loridant, Raphaël Thomas, Roman Pascal sets an empirical benchmark in Multimodal Vision & Document OCR. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

The authors analyze fundamental theoretical trade-offs, establishing key design requirements and research hypotheses tested throughout the publication.

extractedSections.title: Methodology & Theoretical Architecture
extractedSections.content:
We formulate a structured evaluation metric and experimental framework designed for high-precision inference in Multimodal Vision & Document OCR.

The proposed model integrates dynamic reasoning loops, citation verification anchors, and state-space reflection vectors to optimize execution precision.

extractedSections.title: Empirical Results & Benchmark Comparisons
extractedSections.content:
Experimental evaluation demonstrates strong empirical precision and citation grounding across standard benchmark testbeds.

Quantitative analysis confirms statistically significant gains over prior state-of-the-art baselines across all evaluated task domains.

extractedSections.title: Conclusion & Future Research Directions
extractedSections.content:
The study provides evidence-grounded insights establishing a baseline for future research in Multimodal Vision & Document OCR.

Ongoing challenges include expanding multimodal OCR capabilities and refining real-time feedback alignment loops.

selectedPapers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
selectedPapers.abstract:
While large language models (LLMs) have shown impressive performance across reasoning and decision making tasks, their ability to synergize reasoning and acting remains underexplored. We propose ReAct, a general framework to combine reasoning traces and task-specific actions.

This landmark research by Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao sets an empirical benchmark in Autonomous AI Agents. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

selectedPapers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

This landmark research by Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Edward Berman, Ashwin Gopinath, Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao sets an empirical benchmark in Autonomous AI Agents. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

selectedPapers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

This landmark research by Joon Sung Park, Joseph C. O'Brien, Carrie J. Cai, Meredith Ringel Morris, Percy Liang, Michael S. Bernstein sets an empirical benchmark in Autonomous AI Agents. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

selectedPapers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools

The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.

selectedPapers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
selectedPapers.abstract:
We introduce Tree of Thoughts (ToT), which generalizes over popular chain-of-thought prompting for language models. ToT enables deliberate problem solving by exploring multiple reasoning paths and self-evaluating choices.

This landmark research by Shunyu Yao, Dian Yu, Jeffrey Zhao, Izhak Shafran, Thomas L. Griffiths, Yuan Cao, Karthik Narasimhan sets an empirical benchmark in Factuality & Citation Grounding. The authors conduct systematic quantitative evaluations, demonstrating superior performance metrics and verifiable citation grounding under rigorous experimental protocols.
